chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a man departing by night if he is fearful.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man; here, the legally responsible pilgrim
key_terms.بِلَيْلٍ: by night; before the coming of dawn
key_terms.خَائِفًا: fearful; experiencing fear that justifies the concession
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it indicates permissibility
key_terms.يُفِيضَ: to depart or move on ritually from a sacred station during hajj

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to depart from al-Muzdalifah at night before dawn if a person is afraid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning departing from al-Muzdalifah before dawn. It indicates that leaving at night is permissible for someone who has fear, establishing an allowance in a case of hardship or concern.
